extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing and submitting a CIHR Project Grant application (Nominated Principal Applicants, Principal Applicants, Co-Applicants; institutional research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting a CIHR Project Grant application via ResearchNet, including required attachments, formatting, budgeting, participant information, and peer review adjudication standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow CIHR instructions and formatting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing your application, you will need to follow all instructions and requirements including CIHR's formatting guidelines. Failure to follow these instructions may negatively impact the evaluation of your application. CIHR reserves the right to withdraw your application if it does not meet these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere exactly to Acceptable Application Formats and PDF Attachments. ResearchNet may remove content that exceeds page limits (e.g., research proposal pages over the English limit will be removed). Ensure attachments are unsecured where required. Applications not meeting formatting rules risk withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominated Principal Applicant (NPA) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nominated Principal Applicant must remain the same between registration and application and cannot be changed during the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the NPA can submit the application. The NPA must wait for other participants to complete their sections before submitting. The NPA may delegate access to up to five individuals to assist, but should remove delegates prior to final submission. You cannot submit more than two Project Grant applications per competition as an NPA; if you do, CIHR will automatically withdraw the last submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ResearchNet and eApproval process
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use ResearchNet to submit your application(s) and CIHR uses an eApproval process; your institution must approve the application before you submit it to CIHR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Consent and Submit section before the posted deadline. Your application is not legally accepted until eApproval/Consent and Submit are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Self-identification Questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of CIHR's processes, applicants to all CIHR programs must complete an Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Self-identification Questionnaire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All application participants must complete the questionnaire before your internal institutional competition submission deadline. Collaborators are exempt. See FAQs and How-To Instructions for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and page-limit adjustments for French applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit an application in French, you are allowed two additional pages in your research proposal, and attachments for French-language application material will be increased by at least 20%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research proposals: English = 10 pages, French = 12 pages. ResearchNet caps at 12 pages; for English applications any pages beyond 10 may be removed without notice. Summary of Progress: English 2 pages; French 2.5 pages (ResearchNet allows 3 pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained application and attachments (no external hyperlinks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information provided in your application package must be self-contained. Hyperlinks, including links to documents hosted on Google drive or similar, must not be included in any attachments within your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will not access external links. Digital Object Identifiers (DOI) to reference publications are permitted. The research proposal must contain a complete description of the project and all information required to support the research plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) special requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific considerations and formatting requirements apply when a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) is a major component of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the RCT Evaluation Criteria and Headings webpage. Reviewers will take into account RCT-specific considerations during assessment. Note that not all RCTs are clinical trials; indicate both if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Security Guidelines for Research Partnerships (NSGRP) – Risk Assessment Form (RAF)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposal involves one or more private-sector partner organizations, you must complete and upload one Risk Assessment Form (RAF) including a Risk Mitigation Plan as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one RAF per application covering all private-sector partners. Upload as an unsecured PDF under 'Attach Other Application Material'. RAF length limits: 6 pages English, 7 pages French. If no private-sector partners, no RAF required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner / Knowledge User / iKT identification and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether your application includes a partner and/or a knowledge user; if so, identify whether a partner and knowledge user, partner only, or knowledge user only is included and, where required, identify at least one Applicant Partner or a Principal Applicant who is a knowledge user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of a knowledge user does not automatically make it an integrated knowledge translation (iKT) application; answer 'yes' only if the project is a knowledge translation or commercialization project. Applications identified as iKT may be assessed by both researcher and knowledge-user reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if the application contains a clinical trial. CIHR requires clinical trials to be registered and results disclosed publicly in a timely manner per WHO Joint Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult TCPS 2 Chapter 11 and CIHR policy on registration and disclosure. Applicants are encouraged to use mechanisms to support efficient trial start-up (e.g., streamlined REB processes, inter-institutional agreements, participant-focused consent approaches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of sex and gender considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate if sex as a biological variable and/or gender as a socio-cultural factor are taken into account in the research design, methods, analysis, interpretation, and/or dissemination of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, sex and/or gender must be integrated into the research proposal (not only discussed in the textbox). Reviewers will assess integration as a strength, weakness, or not applicable and provide recommendations. Consult CIHR resources on integrating sex/gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptors to assist reviewer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide keywords, themes, suggested institutes, areas of science, methods/approaches, and study populations/experimental systems to inform reviewer assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select primary and up to allowed additional classifications where applicable; rank multiple selections in order of relevance. Use provided reference documents for valid choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal content and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a research proposal that is stand-alone and contains a complete description of the project; page limits: English 10 pages, French 12 pages. References are a separate attachment and do not count toward the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within page limits you may include text, tables, charts, figures and photographs. Use the adjudication criteria to structure the proposal. Follow formatting requirements exactly; CIHR may withdraw applications that do not comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Progress attachment and content
rubrics_metrics.description: All Nominated Principal Applicants must attach a Summary of Progress: English 2 pages; French 2.5 pages (ResearchNet allows 3 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrative should describe how the application fits within your program of research, outline progress/productivity/impact, provide ECR-specific narrative if applicable, discuss impacts on progress (e.g., leaves, pandemic), and contextualize the requested budget relative to other funding. Do not use this as an extension of the research proposal; do not include figures, tables or hyperlinks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation scoring and reviewer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application will be rated by three reviewers on a scale of 0.0 to 4.9, with 4.9 being the highest possible rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers use the adjudication criteria and interpretation guidelines. Committee assignment is determined by CIHR; suggested reviewers/committees provided by applicants are advisory only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 1 – Concept: Significance and Impact of Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the quality of what is proposed, the value of anticipated contributions, and advances in health-related knowledge, health care, health systems, and/or health outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review questions include: Is the project idea creative? Is the rationale sound? Are goals and objectives well-defined and aligned to outputs? Are anticipated contributions substantive, realistic, and relevant to the described context and gaps? IHR committee adds: relevance to First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis priorities and potential to produce valued outcomes for Indigenous peoples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 2.1 – Approaches and Methods (Assessment of Feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the quality of the project's design and plan, including how and when the project will be completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Are approaches/methods appropriate and justified to deliver outputs and contributions? Is sex/gender integration addressed? Are timelines and deliverables realistic and aligned with objectives? Are potential challenges identified with realistic mitigation strategies? IHR committee: approaches must respect Indigenous values/ways of knowing and relevant ethical guidelines (TCPS2 Chapter 9) or explain alternatives agreed with governance bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 2.2 – Expertise, Experience and Resources (Assessment of Feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the team and environment have the appropriate expertise, experience, commitment and resources to collectively deliver the proposed outputs and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimated hours per week (contribution) for each applicant. Describe roles/responsibilities linked to objectives, level of engagement/time commitment, institutional environment, infrastructure, equipment, and support. Demonstrate productivity and progress in the Summary of Progress. IHR committee: evaluate team relevance including Indigenous research experience and track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach Project References rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The only permitted attachment for references is a PDF list of references cited within your application, in a standard reference style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual publications or other documents are not acceptable as references attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required 'Attach other application material' documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain attachments are mandatory where applicable: SGBA+ training certificate (NPA only), Risk Assessment Form (if private-sector partners), letter of support for pending appointment, letter of community support for Indigenous partner(s), employer attestation for paid international researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow file format/unsecured PDF instructions where specified. Observe document count and page limits for each required attachment (e.g., SGBA+ limit one one-page document; RAF limits noted earlier; community letters up to 20 documents of up to 5 pages each).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted and not-accepted optional attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: May attach letters of collaboration (up to 99 documents, up to 5 pages each) describing specific services. Certain documents are not accepted and will be removed: Patient Information Sheet (for RCTs), Publications, Questionnaires/surveys/consent forms, Supplementary tables/charts/figures/photographs, Cost quotations, CVs, Any other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of collaboration must not be extensions of the research proposal or contain documentation no longer accepted. Ensure optional attachments do not duplicate proposal content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Application Partners – partner letter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For partners providing cash and/or in-kind contributions, provide a signed letter of support from every partner at time of application specifying specific incremental cash or in-kind contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter partner information in the Identify Application Partners task, select partner from CIHR prepopulated list or create a new organization record, and upload the partner's signed PDF letter under Manage Attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget totals and currency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All amounts entered in the budget must be totals for the entire duration of the grant (not yearly amounts) and should be in Canadian dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR will divide total equally across years. Each amount must be rounded to a multiple of $1,000. The sum of all budget categories must be a multiple of $5,000. Do not include cost quotations as part of the application. Budget should include applicable provincial and federal taxes calculated using after-rebate tax rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification and category-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed justification for each budget category describing what funds will be used for and why they are required in relation to planned activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum 3,500 characters per category; justification only saves if requested amount is entered. Categories include Research Staff (detail FTEs, roles, salaries), Trainees (number, roles, salaries), Consumables (direct costs only; no indirect costs), Non-Consumables (equipment definition: >$2,000 and useful life >1 year; include maintenance/operating costs), Knowledge Translation (dissemination costs), and Other. For Indigenous-involving projects, eligible costs include community mobilization, culturally relevant items, reimbursements and contracts for Indigenous knowledge keepers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner Budget Details subtask
rubrics_metrics.description: If partners are involved and will contribute funds, you must complete the Partner Budget Details subtask to list cash and in-kind contributions by year and describe how they will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include partner funding in budget after identifying the partner in the Partner Task. Enter zero for years with no contribution. Provide up to 900 characters to describe use per partner per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review administration: suggested and excluded reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: You are encouraged to suggest at least 5 Canadian and/or international reviewers and may provide names of individuals to exclude with justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suggest reviewers with whom you have a conflict of interest. CIHR makes final selection of reviewers. Suggested committees and justifications are advisory; CIHR will consult Chairs and Scientific Officers and make the final assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview, Manage Access, and Consent and Submit procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You are strongly encouraged to preview the full application before submitting. NPA can delegate access to up to five individuals and revoke access. All Principal Applicants and Co-Applicants must consent to terms before NPA can submit; NPA clicks 'Submit to CIHR' to initiate eApproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preview task can be marked complete only when all other tasks are complete. Delegates’ access does not persist through all competition phases; NPA should remove delegates prior to Consent and Submit. After submission, the application is sent to the Institution Paid and then CIHR; confirmation email is sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIHR expectations on assessing productivity and DORA guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR is a signatory of DORA; reviewers are instructed to assess productivity broadly (not only publication metrics) and not to use journal-based metrics like Journal Impact Factor as surrogates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should highlight a broad range of contributions and impacts (publications, datasets, code, training, policy influence, community engagement, commercialization, etc.) and reviewers should consider context (leave history, career stage, diverse career paths, pandemic impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization and Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review special processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications submitted to the Commercialization committee must be structured according to provided headings. Applications to the Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review committee undergo a unique peer review process and are evaluated against specific criteria within the Project Grant adjudication framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Committee Peer Review Guide and Section 5 of the peer review guide for details on specific evaluation criteria and interpretation for these committees.
